items.title: Section: Precept Six — Sharing the Teaching With Genuine Seekers

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，他來求法，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，嫉妬變異，不施其法，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若由嬾惰、懈怠、忘念、無記之心，不施其法，是名有犯，有所違越，非染違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, approached by a genuine seeker of the teaching, who, out of resentment, irritation, or jealousy, refuse to give it — this constitutes a tainted violation.

items.zh: 無違犯者，謂諸外道伺求過短；或有重病；或心狂亂；或欲方便調彼、伏彼，出不善處安立善處；或於是法未善通利；或復見彼不生恭敬，無有羞愧，以惡威儀而來聽受；或復知彼是鈍根性，於廣法教得法究竟深生怖畏，當生邪見，增長邪執，衰損惱壞；或復知彼，法至其手轉布非人；而不施與，皆無違犯。
items.en: There is no violation towards a hostile outsider seeking only to find fault; one who is genuinely ill or mentally deranged; one being deliberately corrected through this withholding; a teaching not yet genuinely mastered oneself; a seeker showing no respect or shame in their manner; one whose limited capacity would only give rise to wrong view and worsening harm from teaching too advanced for them; or one likely to pass the scripture on to unworthy hands.

items.title: Section: Precept Seven Closes — Never Abandoning Even a Violent Wrongdoer

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，於諸暴惡犯戒有情，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，由彼暴惡犯戒為緣，方便棄捨，不作饒益，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, harbouring resentment or irritation towards a violently precept-breaking being, deliberately abandon them and refuse to help — this constitutes a tainted violation.

items.zh: 若由嬾惰懈怠棄捨，由忘念故，不作饒益，是名有犯，有所違越，非染違犯。
何以故？非諸菩薩於淨持戒、身語意業寂靜現行諸有情所，起憐愍心，欲作饒益；如於暴惡犯戒有情，於諸苦因而現轉者。
items.en: Why is this? Because a bodhisattva's compassion towards beings of already calm, disciplined conduct is not meant to exceed their compassion towards violently precept-breaking beings actively creating the very causes of their own future suffering.

items.zh: 無違犯者，謂心狂亂；或欲方便調彼、伏彼，廣說如前；或為將護多有情心；或護僧制；方便棄捨，不作饒益，皆無違犯。

items.title: Section: Discipline-Progression Opens — Observing the Restrictive Precepts Shared With Śrāvakas

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，如薄伽梵於別解脫毘奈耶中，將護他故，建立遮罪，制諸聲聞令不造作。諸有情類，未淨信者令生淨信，已淨信者令倍增長。於中菩薩與諸聲聞應等修學，無有差別。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts should observe exactly as the Blessed One established within the individually liberating monastic code — restrictive precepts established in order to protect others, so that those without faith come to have it, and those with faith have it deepened further. In this matter, bodhisattvas should train exactly as śrāvakas do, without any difference.

items.zh: 何以故？以諸聲聞自利為勝，尚不棄捨將護他行，為令有情未信者信、信者增長，學所學處，何況菩薩利他為勝。
items.en: Why is this? Because śrāvakas, who prioritise their own liberation, still do not abandon protecting others through their own visible conduct, training in these precepts so that faith arises and deepens in those who witness them — how much more so, then, should bodhisattvas, who prioritise benefiting others above all, uphold this same practice.

items.title: Section: Precept Nine — Why a Bodhisattva May Accumulate What a Śrāvaka Must Renounce

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，如薄伽梵於別解脫毘奈耶中，為令聲聞少事、少業、少悕望住，建立遮罪，制諸聲聞令不造作。於中菩薩與諸聲聞不應等學。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts, unlike śrāvakas, are not bound by the restrictive precepts the Blessed One established within the monastic code specifically to cultivate few possessions, few undertakings, and minimal desire. In this matter, bodhisattvas should not train exactly as śrāvakas do.

items.zh: 何以故？以諸聲聞自利為勝，不顧利他，於利他中少事、少業、少悕望住可名為妙；非諸菩薩利他為勝，不顧自利，於利他中少事、少業、少悕望住得名為妙。如是菩薩為利他故，從非親里長者、居士、婆羅門等及恣施家，應求百千種種衣服，觀彼有情有力無力，隨其所施，如應而受。如說求衣，求鉢亦爾。如求衣鉢，如是自求種種絲縷，令非親里為織作衣。為利他故，應畜種種憍世耶衣、諸坐臥具，事各至百，生色可染百千俱胝，復過是數亦應取積。
items.en: Why is this? Because śrāvakas prioritise their own liberation, not the benefit of others ... whereas bodhisattvas, for the sake of benefiting others, may rightly request hundreds and thousands of garments even from unrelated donors and generous households ... and may accumulate even vast quantities of gold and silver beyond that, and rightly gather it all in.

items.zh: 如是等中少事、少業、少悕望住制止遮罪，菩薩不與聲聞共學。安住淨戒律儀菩薩，於利他中，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，少事、少業、少悕望住，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。若由嬾惰、懈怠、忘念、無記之心，少事、少業、少悕望住，是名有犯，有所違越，非染違犯。

items.title: Section: When Compassion Overrides an Ordinary Precept — The Classical Doctrine of Skilful Exception

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，善權方便，為利他故，於諸性罪少分現行，由是因緣，於菩薩戒無所違犯，生多功德。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts, through skilful judgement and purely for the sake of benefiting others, perform, only in partial form, what would ordinarily constitute one of the classically wrong deeds — through this very cause, they incur no violation of the bodhisattva precepts at all, and instead generate substantial merit.

blocks.text: More lighter precepts, then the start of one of the most discussed passages in Mahāyāna ethics: when compassion may require breaking an ordinary rule. A short passage (0517a28) is untranslated.
Refusing a genuine seeker "out of resentment or jealousy" is tainted. No offence towards an outsider seeking only to find fault, or when withholding is meant as correction.

Abandoning "a violently precept-breaking being" out of resentment is tainted, "because a bodhisattva's compassion towards the well-behaved should not exceed their compassion towards wrongdoers". Master Cháng Bǎi: like a mother caring most for her sickest child.

Where the Buddha set rules to protect others' faith, "bodhisattvas should train exactly as śrāvakas do". Where rules exist to help monks need little, bodhisattvas, "for the sake of others", may ask for many robes and bowls to give away. Venerable Miào Jìng: they live with many affairs, but still with few desires.

subs.head: Four ways of using what is given

blocks.text: (Untranslated in full.) Like a thief (using offerings while breaking precepts); like a debtor (keeping precepts but lacking wisdom); like an heir (a trainee); like a master (an arhat or great bodhisattva).

"Through skilful judgement and purely for the sake of benefiting others", a bodhisattva may perform, "in partial form", what is ordinarily a natural wrong, "and incurs no violation, but generates great merit". Venerable Miào Jìng: "partial" because affliction, one of the five factors of a complete deed, is absent. Master Cháng Bǎi notes the traditional debate about who may do this: Daoxuan said only bodhisattvas of the Dharma body and above; Fazang, those at the first abode who dwell in non-self; Ouyi, both ordinary and noble beings. This is not a licence for ordinary practitioners.

quiz.q: Withholding the teaching out of resentment is tainted. Which is an exemption?
options: an outsider seeking only to find fault
quiz.why: "There is no violation towards a hostile outsider seeking only to find fault," among others. Master Cháng Bǎi: seeking the dharma is of two kinds — asking the bodhisattva to teach, or asking for scriptures.

quiz.q: One must not abandon violent wrongdoers. Whose story of going to subdue a wrongdoer does Venerable Miào Jìng tell?
options: Venerable Xūyún, on hearing of it, went to him on his own initiative to subdue him
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: such beings urgently need the bodhisattva's protection — Venerable Xūyún, learning of such a person, went to him on his own to subdue him. Master Cháng Bǎi uses the image of a mother caring most for her sickest child.

quiz.q: Restrictive precepts the Buddha set up "to protect others" — how should bodhisattvas train in them?
options: train exactly as śrāvakas do, without difference
quiz.why: "In this matter, bodhisattvas should train exactly as [śrāvakas] do, without any difference" — since even those who put their own liberation first do not neglect protecting others' faith, how much more bodhisattvas, who put others first.

quiz.q: Restrictive precepts set up so śrāvakas may "dwell with few affairs, few undertakings, few wishes" — how do bodhisattvas train in them?
options: bodhisattvas should not train as śrāvakas do
quiz.why: "In this matter, bodhisattvas should not train exactly as [śrāvakas] do." Master Cháng Bǎi: dhūta (ascetic practice) is rendered "shaking off" — rousing oneself to practise.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas may seek and accumulate much for others' sake. How does Venerable Miào Jìng contrast the bodhisattva's way of living?
options: bodhisattvas should dwell with many affairs, many undertakings, many wishes
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: bodhisattvas should dwell with many affairs, undertakings, and wishes — yet still observe whether the donor can afford it. Master Cháng Bǎi: if it exceeds the donor's means, the bodhisattva does not accept.

quiz.q: The English renders "shǎo fēn xiànxíng" as "occasionally and only in small degree." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "shǎo fēn"?
options: among the conditions for a complete course of action, the fourth — affliction — is missing, hence "partial"; it is not about frequency or degree
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the fourth factor, affliction, is not present. Following the 《披尋記》, of the five factors of a course of action, affliction is missing — hence "partial." The English reads it as frequency and degree.

quiz.q: To what level of bodhisattva does this exception apply? Whose views does Master Cháng Bǎi list?
options: Daoxuan: only bodhisattvas of the dharma body and above; Fazang: first-abode bodhisattvas abiding in selflessness; Ouyi: both ordinary and noble
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: Vinaya Master Daoxuan held that the exception for the seven bodily and verbal acts applies only to bodhisattvas of the dharma body and above; Fazang, to first-abode bodhisattvas abiding in selflessness; Ouyi, to both ordinary and noble beings.
